```{r setup}
suppressMessages(library(lme4))
out <- "stata_recreation_output"
if (!file.exists(file.path(out, "eb_stata_recreation.rds"))) source("teney_stata_recreation.R")
eb <- readRDS(file.path(out, "eb_stata_recreation.rds"))
eb$wave_f <- factor(eb$eb)

show_model <- function(f) {
  m <- lmer(as.formula(f), data = eb, REML = FALSE)
  cat(f, "\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("N = %d", nobs(m)), paste0(names(ngrps(m)), " = ", ngrps(m), collapse = ", "), "\n\n")
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m))
  print(data.frame(group = vc$grp, sd = round(vc$sdcor, 4)), row.names = FALSE)
  s <- summary(m)$coefficients
  cat("\n")
  print(data.frame(b = round(s[, 1], 5), se = round(s[, 2], 5), z = round(s[, 3], 2),
                   p = signif(2 * pnorm(-abs(s[, 3])), 2)))
}

fx <- "cos ~ female + mage + edu3 + ses + urban + mgrowth + munemp + mgrowth:edu3 + munemp:edu3"
```

All models below use the data built by `teney_stata_recreation.R`: EB 80.1–91.5 (2013–2019), coded as in Teney's Stata files (`original_script/eb_all.do`, `original_script/eb_ml_ESR.do`), fitted by maximum likelihood without weights. The focal coefficient is `munemp`, the unemployment slope for the low-educated at the grand mean. In 2004–2013 it was b = −0.00340, t = −4.03.

# Code conversion: Teney (Stata) → ours (R)

### Outcome

The outcome is the share of mentioned items that are cosmopolitan; "Euro" is left out of the denominator.

Teney (Stata):

```stata
gen sumeu=peace+eco_pros+demo+soc_prot+trav+div+say+unemp+bur+waste+loss_id+crime+border
gen cos=(peace/sumeu)+(demo/sumeu)+(trav/sumeu)+(div/sumeu)+(say/sumeu)
```

Ours (R):

```r
sumeu = peace + eco_pros + demo + soc_prot + trav + div + say + unemp +
        bur + waste + loss_id + crime + border
cos = (peace + demo + trav + div + say) / sumeu
# x/0 -> NA, as Stata returns missing
```

For comparison, the replication (`teney.R`) instead takes the mean of the five cosmopolitan dummies, i.e. count ÷ 5:

```r
mutate(cosmo = rowMeans(.[, c('qa12_1', 'qa12_3', 'qa12_5', 'qa12_6', 'qa12_7')], na.rm = TRUE))
```

### Education

Students get their current age, and "no full-time education" is set to missing. Stata ranks missing above every number, so `edu>19` also puts missing education in the high group. The R script copies this by default (`STATA_MISSING_EDU_IS_HIGH`).

Teney (Stata):

```stata
replace edu=age if edu==98
replace edu=. if edu==97
replace edu3=1 if edu<16
replace edu3=2 if edu==16|edu==17|edu==18|edu==19
replace edu3=3 if edu>19
```

Ours (R):

```r
edu[edu %in% 98] <- age[edu %in% 98]
edu[edu %in% 97] <- NA
edu3[edu < 16]              <- 1
edu3[edu >= 16 & edu <= 19] <- 2
edu3[edu > 19]              <- 3
if (STATA_MISSING_EDU_IS_HIGH) edu3[is.na(edu)] <- 3
```

### Grand-mean centring

Teney hard-coded the means of her own sample. The R script uses the means of the new sample.

Teney (Stata):

```stata
gen munemp=unemp_rate-8.76
gen mgrowth=growth-1.41
gen mage=age-48
```

Ours (R):

```r
munemp  <- unemp_rate - mean(unemp_rate)
mgrowth <- growth     - mean(growth)
mage    <- age        - mean(age)
```

### Model and random effects

Teney's level 2 is the country-wave (`eb_ctr`), nested within country.

Teney (Stata):

```stata
mixed cos female mage i.edu3 b4.ses b3.urban mgrowth munemp c.mgrowth##edu3 c.munemp##edu3
  || cty: || eb_ctr: if eb!=203 & eb!=303 & eb!=906, covariance(unstructured)
```

Ours (R):

```r
lmer(cos ~ female + mage + edu3 + ses + urban + mgrowth + munemp +
       mgrowth:edu3 + munemp:edu3 + (1 | cty_f) + (1 | eb_ctr_f),
     data = eb, REML = FALSE)
# ses ref = manual workers, urban ref = large town
```

The replication has no country-wave level. It fits crossed wave and country intercepts, uses uncentred unemployment and GDP, adds both squared terms, and weights the data:

```r
lmer(cosmo ~ 1 + d11 + d10 + d8r2 + relevel(d25, ref = "3") +
       relevel(d15a_r2, ref = "4") + UNEMPL + I(UNEMPL^2) + GDP + I(GDP^2) +
       d8r2*GDP + d8r2*UNEMPL + (1 | wave1) + (1 | country),
     data = final.merge4, REML = FALSE, weights = w1)
```

Unemployment and growth vary only between country-waves (378 of them), not between respondents. Without a country-wave intercept, the model treats every respondent as a separate observation of those macro variables, so their standard errors are too small. Model 4 below shows what this does to the squared term.

**Data.** Croatia is not in Teney's country list, so it is dropped. Her country-level file (`var_cty.dta`) is not available, so unemployment and real GDP growth are Eurostat annual values (`une_rt_a`, `tec00115`) for the survey year.

# Models

## 1. Teney's model (Table 3, cosmopolitan)

Random intercepts for country and for country-wave nested within country.

```{r}
show_model(paste(fx, "+ (1 | cty_f) + (1 | eb_ctr_f)"))
```

## 2. With a squared unemployment term, run as decribed in Teney's paper

Same random effects as model 1.

```{r}
show_model(paste(fx, "+ I(munemp^2) + (1 | cty_f) + (1 | eb_ctr_f)"))
```

## 3. Teney's procedure: keep only the significant squared terms

Teney added squared terms for the macro variables and kept only the significant ones. Her `eb_ml_ESR.do` note says that for the cosmopolitan frame they were "ns", so she kept none. The 2013–2019 data have two macro variables, unemployment and growth. Step 1 adds both squared terms to model 1:

```{r}
m_both <- lmer(as.formula(paste(fx, "+ I(munemp^2) + I(mgrowth^2) + (1 | cty_f) + (1 | eb_ctr_f)")),
               data = eb, REML = FALSE)
s <- summary(m_both)$coefficients[c("I(munemp^2)", "I(mgrowth^2)"), ]
print(data.frame(b = round(s[, 1], 5), se = round(s[, 2], 5), z = round(s[, 3], 2),
                 p = signif(2 * pnorm(-abs(s[, 3])), 2)))
```

Step 2 drops the non-significant squared term (unemployment), keeps squared growth, and refits:

```{r}
show_model(paste(fx, "+ I(mgrowth^2) + (1 | cty_f) + (1 | eb_ctr_f)"))
```

## 4. With the squared term and the replication's random effects

Crossed random intercepts for wave and country, with no country-wave level. This is the replication's random-effects structure, applied to Teney's coding.

```{r}
show_model(paste(fx, "+ I(munemp^2) + (1 | wave_f) + (1 | cty_f)"))
```
